> **Tracking epic — NOT directly implementable.** Roadie: implement the phase issues, not this one. If you picked this up, stop and output `NEEDS_HUMAN: tracking epic, implement phase issues instead`.

## Mission (founder-approved 2026-07-16)

Turn `/bands/<slug>` pages from thin stubs into **the** authority on each band's drum chair: who played, when, on which albums, with what gear. Wikipedia has lineups, Equipboard has gear, Drummerworld has bios — nobody joins them by era. We can.

## Evidence this is the right surface

- 35 bands in `bands.js`, but only 4 have FAQs, 3 have full lineups, 3 have discographies — most pages render from ~6 thin fields.
- Zero `/bands/` URLs earn ranked queries in L1; zero appear in the L3 indexation sample. The pages exist but don't compete.
- GSC shows the intent we're missing: "john otto band", "nick augusto band", "mikkey dee bands" — and the inverse class "**who is the drummer of <band>**" (searcher doesn't know the name yet) is winnable only by a band page, and is a classic LLM question (L2 KPI).
- Head terms ("metallica") are unwinnable; the drummer-intent middle ("slipknot drummer history", "who drummed on Iowa") is high-intent and links directly to our money pages.

## Phases

1. Phase 1 — enrich all 35 existing band entries (verified lineups, FAQ, discography with drummer-per-album) + fix llms/bands drift (19/35)
2. Phase 2 — drum-chair timeline UI on `/bands/<slug>` + data-driven FAQ/meta
3. Phase 3 — expand 35 → ~70 bands (every roster drummer's bands + top-searched metal bands)
4. Phase 4 — query capture: watched queries, internal links, full `/llms/bands/` coverage, L2 targets

## Binding rules (apply to EVERY phase — copy of the standing theme-hub rules + band-specific)

1. **ONE data module.** `packages/frontend/data/bands.js` is the single source of truth. Never create a second bands data file; API/meta/sitemap/llms all derive from it by import (as today).
2. **Tenure verification (the #4160 lesson).** Any drummer-per-album or lineup claim must confirm the drummer was a member **during that album's recording/release window** — a name appearing near an album title in a blurb is NOT evidence (Kairos was recorded by Jean Dolabella, not Eloy Casagrande, despite the timeline mention). Check join/leave dates against recording dates.
3. **Verified-only, omit-if-unsure.** Every fact needs a source (Wikipedia / MusicBrainz / band or label site). An entry with a missing verified field ships without that field — never with a guess.
4. **No fabricated URLs.** `sameAs` links must resolve; no invented article/retailer links. New bands require `sameAs` with at least Wikipedia + MusicBrainz or Wikidata.
5. **URLs are immutable.** The scheme stays `/bands/<slug>`; enrichment is additive on existing pages.
6. **llms mirrors derive from the module.** Whatever generates `/llms/bands/*.md` must iterate `Object.keys(bands)` — the current 19-of-35 drift is exactly the hardcoded-list failure this rule prevents.
7. **Measure, don't assume.** Phase 4 adds the target query class to `watched-queries.json` so L1 verifies the bet.
title: EPIC: /bands drum-chair history — Tokyo theme area #5 (the authority on who drummed, when, on which albums)
